title: info
description: The shared documents (plan 027 §3.3): the session info document, the sessions.list row, both capability sets, the hub's roster row (plan 032 §3.6), and the pieces they share.

sessionInfoFields.description: The session info document's members, shared by sessionInfo and sessionRow.

sessionId.description: The durable craze session id: what every session-scoped method names.

providerSessionId.description: The agent's own id for the session; may be "" before the session is ready.

incarnation.description: The event log's id: the scope of seqs, turn ids and ask ids.

startedAt.description: When the host started serving the session, in UTC: what a client counts elapsed time from. Absent when the host does not say (an older host).

sessionInfo.description: The session info document: the session's static facts, final once the session is up (the attach reply's session, a ready notification's). Its catalogs are empty until then.

sessionRow.description: One sessions.list row: the info document and the session's live roster facts. "Is it running" is activity == working or foreignTurn; "is it blocked on me" is pendingAsks > 0.

foreignTurn.description: The agent is running a turn of its own; activity reads idle during one.

doing.description: A row fact (capabilities.rowFacts): what a working session is doing — the title of the most recently started tool of the running turn still running, else Responding while the agent's text streams, else Thinking. Present only while a turn (craze's own or a foreign one) is working.

lastReply.description: A row fact: the first line of the last completed assistant message; absent when there is none.

since.description: A row fact: when the row entered its current state — the first of needs you (pendingAsks > 0), failed (startFailed, or lastTurn.outcome failed, or activity error with neither lastTurn nor foreignTurn: a failure whose ending is still on its way), working (activity starting, replaying, working or closing, or foreignTurn), idle — on the host's clock, in UTC.

startFailed.description: A row fact: the session's start failed. Absent is false on a rowFacts host.

startErr.description: A row fact: the first line of a failed start's error.

prompted.description: A row fact: a turn has been started at all. Absent is false on a rowFacts host.

model.description: A row fact (plan 035): the session's current model id, exact — session.state's settings.model, what a session.set of kind model names — not display text, and never cut: unbounded, as settings.model is. Absent means unknown on any host, a rowFacts host from before plan 035 included.

attached.description: Where the session capability presence is true: how many clients are attached to the session as the row is read — every attachment the host counts (pending, live or closing, not one whose peer has half-closed) and, on a TUI-hosted session, the hosting TUI's own seat. Absent is 0 on a presence host, and unknown on any other.

provider.description: The session's provider: its id and the label a client shows.

catalogs.description: The models and modes the session can be switched to; empty until the session is ready. models is the list as the document is built, which a native session's reload changes while it runs; revision numbers it, as the event stream's catalog section does.

revision.description: The revision of models: the catalog section's that last changed it. Absent while 0 — the list the session started with, every ACP session's, and every older host's. A client that also folds the stream's catalog section shows whichever list is newer by revision, never an older one.

model.description: One model a session.set of kind model can name.

recent.description: The model's rank in the native provider's model memory: 1 for the most recently picked model the session offers, then 2, 3 and so on. Absent for a model not remembered, for every ACP provider's model, and on an older host. A client lists the remembered models right after the current one, by rank.

efforts.description: The effort levels the model offers, in order: one of its effort facts, stated where the session capability effortFacts is true (a native session). Absent for a model with no effort control, for every ACP provider's model, and on an older host. A client reads the current model's effort from its effort option, never from this row.

defaultEffort.description: The model's default effort, one of efforts. Absent for a model with none, for every ACP provider's model, and on an older host.

switchEffort.description: The effort a switch to the model lands on, one of efforts: the session's own last choice on it, else the one the model memory remembers, else its default. Absent for a model with no effort control, for every ACP provider's model, and on an older host.

mode.description: One mode a session.set of kind mode can name.

sessionCapabilities.description: The session's capability set: every provider capability in its wire name, and cancel, approvals, historyCursor (true for every protocol 1 host), stop (the host's own: true where session.stop is served, every craze serve; false on a TUI-hosted session and an older host), rowFacts (the host's own, omitted when false: the row carries the row facts), presence (the host's own, omitted when false: the host sends presence and the row carries attached), and the session's own modelsRefresh and aside (each omitted when false: the host serves the methods they name), slashCatalog (omitted when false: the session publishes the slash catalog section) and effortFacts (omitted when false: every catalog model states its effort facts), and exitAfterTurn (the host's own, omitted when false: session.prompt takes exitAfterTurn and session.stop takes cause). A client hides what a capability says the session cannot do.

rowFacts.description: The host's own: the session's sessions.list row carries the row facts (headAsk.summary, doing, lastReply, since, startFailed, startErr, prompted). Absent — false — on an older host, whose row is read as it was.

presence.description: The host's own: the host counts the clients attached to the session, sends each attachment the presence notification, and puts attached on the session's sessions.list row. Absent — false — on an older host, which sends no presence: a client shows no count.

modelsRefresh.description: The session can take up models funded while it runs (a native session), and the host serves session.models.refresh for it. Absent — false — for an ACP session, and on an older host: the method is refused there, and a client makes no call.

aside.description: The session answers side questions (/btw) from its context (a native, grok or gx session), and the host serves session.aside and session.aside.cancel for it. Absent — false — for cursor, and on an older host: the methods are refused there, and a client offers no side questions.

slashCatalog.description: The session publishes the slash catalog (a cursor, grok, gx or native session): the state delta's slash section, and the snapshot's settings.slash — every / row it offers and what running each does. Absent — false — on an older host and for a session that is not craze's own: a client offers no / menu from the stream.

effortFacts.description: Every model of the session's catalog states its effort facts (a native session): catalogs.models and the catalog section's models carry efforts, defaultEffort and switchEffort, and a model with no effort control lists none. Absent — false — for an ACP session, on an older host and for a session that is not craze's own: a client shows only the current model's levels, from its effort option.

exitAfterTurn.description: The host's own: session.prompt takes exitAfterTurn and session.stop takes cause, on a host that serves session.stop. It fences what craze admits, not a turn an agent starts entirely on its own. Absent — false — on a TUI-hosted session and an older host, which refuse both members, and a client sends neither.

connectionCapabilities.description: The connection's capability set (hello's). On a host: rosterSubscribe, sessionCreate, multiplex and connect are false; snapshot and attachWhenNow are true; createOptions is absent. On the hub: rosterSubscribe and connect are true; multiplex, snapshot and attachWhenNow false; sessionCreate true where the hub serves session.create; createOptions true where it serves sessions.createOptions, and absent otherwise; createTitle true where its session.create takes a title, and absent otherwise; reopen true where it serves sessions.saved and session.reopen both, and absent otherwise.

createOptions.description: The hub's, omitted when false: the hub serves sessions.createOptions. Absent — false — on a host, on a hub from before it existed, and on one given no answer to it: a client makes no call.

createTitle.description: The hub's, omitted when false: its session.create takes a title. Absent — false — on a host and on a hub from before it existed, which refuses a create naming one unknown_field: a client that has a title to set checks it first.

reopen.description: The hub's, omitted when false: the hub serves sessions.saved and session.reopen both, a client's resume of a saved session. Absent — false — on a host, on a hub from before it existed and on one given no answer to either: a client hides its resume entry.

retryHorizon.description: The command-id table's bound: within it a resent commandId is answered from the table and never re-executes; past it, unknown_command.

headAsk.description: The first open ask: its id, kind (permission, question or plan) and the label a card draws — and, on a sessions.list row of a rowFacts host, its summary.

summary.description: A row fact: what the ask is about — a permission's command or tool title, a question's first question, a plan's name. Absent when there is none, and never on session.state.

rowText.description: A row fact's text: one line — the first non-blank one, tabs expanded — of at most 200 terminal cells, an ellipsis ending one that was cut.

activity.description: What the engine is doing. An open ask and a foreign turn overlay any of these.

permissionMode.description: How the host's agent handles permission requests: bypass (spawned with --force: it runs tools unasked) or prompt (--no-force: it asks, and a client answers). Absent when the host does not say (an older host).

lastTurn.description: How the session's last turn ended — a turn of craze's own or a foreign one. Absent while a turn runs (a turn starting supersedes it), before any has ended, and from an older host. Never in a snapshot.

err.description: A failed turn's error text; absent for the other outcomes.

stopReason.description: The ending's own stop reason: absent for a foreign turn, a failure with none, and an older host.

cause.description: On a stopReason of closing: what began the session's close, one of stop, signal, idle, exit_after_turn or lost_owner. Absent otherwise, from an older host, and when a terminal closed its own session.

withdrawn.description: A cancelled turn's prompt never reached the agent, so no step of it ran. Absent otherwise, and from an older host.

kind.description: What the failure said of itself where it happened, one of the kinds in the CLI reference; absent from a host that predates it, which a reader takes for unknown.

retryable.description: A fresh turn may succeed. Absent is false.

status.description: The provider's HTTP status; absent for none. An ACP agent's JSON-RPC code is not one.

provider_code.description: The provider's own short name for the failure; absent for none.

endedAt.description: The turn's ending event's time, in UTC.

turnId.description: The ended turn's id as the stream names it: turn.id for a turn of craze's own, the foreign_turn bracket's id for the agent's own.

turnOutcome.description: done: ran to its end (a foreign turn's ending is always done); failed: its ending carried an error; cancelled: stopped before its end — a cancel, a prompt withdrawn before it was sent, or the session's close.

rosterRow.description: One row of the hub's roster (plan 032 §3.6): what the hub knows about one host, keyed by hostId, and the host's own sessions.list row. A host without a craze session id is not listed. No socket path crosses the wire. Every member is bounded, so a whole roster row encodes to at most 32,000 bytes (protocol.RosterEntryBytesMax): the hub cuts an over-long host string to its bound, drops a host row over 16 KiB, and drops the row of a roster row still over 32,000 bytes, marking each such roster row approximate.

hostId.description: The host's id: the row's key, stable from the host's first registry appearance.

sessionId.description: The host's craze session id: what session.connect and craze bridge --session take. A host whose craze session id is not such a token is not listed.

approximate.description: The row is not fresh — its last successful read is more than 3 s old, or the host is not reachable — or the hub cut or dropped something to keep it within its bounds.

forwardedRow.description: A host's own sessions.list row (sessionRow) as that host sent it, passed through the hub as a JSON value: any object, since the members a newer host adds — at any depth — pass through untouched. This build's sessionRow describes the members it knows, and a client reads the row tolerantly. Absent until the hub's first read of the host; while it is unreachable, the last row read. At most 16 KiB encoded (protocol.RosterRowBytesMax).

rosterHost.description: What the hub knows about a host beside its row: its registry entry's pid, protocol, provider name, workspace, start time and readiness, and its hello's craze version. Each string is bounded in characters (protocol.RosterCrazeVersionMax, RosterProviderMax, RosterWorkspaceMax); the hub cuts a longer one to its bound and marks the roster row approximate.

crazeVersion.description: From the host's hello; "" until the hub's first hello to it.

rosterStatus.description: Whether the hub reaches the host: connecting until its first attempt, then reachable (the last attempt read the row) or unreachable (it failed; row is the last one read, if any).
